variants.name: View object + presenter module
variants.idiom_name: plain object/class implementing the view methods + presenter factory/module using addEventListener
variants.implementation_notes: JavaScript's duck typing removes the interface: the presenter is a module or factory that receives a view object with methods (query(), showTotal(total)), the view forwards DOM events by calling the presenter, and a test double is a plain object literal - which is why the classic structure is replaced rather than reproduced. Keep DOM access, formatting of widgets and event registration inside the view module, and keep the presenter free of DOM imports so it runs under plain Node test runners. The classic view class hierarchy is only justified when one presenter must drive several genuinely different widget trees.
pitfalls: Listeners must be removable: keep the handler reference or an AbortController signal, otherwise a torn-down screen keeps its closures (and the model) alive.
Passing an object method as a callback detaches it from its receiver; bind once (const refresh = ... or callbacks that are arrow functions closing over the view).
A view module that imports the model directly re-couples the layers; only the presenter may touch both sides.

variants.name: Custom element as the passive view
variants.idiom_name: HTMLElement subclass with semantic methods + connectedCallback wiring; presenter attached by the host
variants.implementation_notes: The view can be a Web Component: a class extending HTMLElement that exposes the screen's semantic operations as methods and forwards its DOM events to whatever presenter the host attaches, with connectedCallback/disconnectedCallback giving the browser-managed attach/detach hooks the pattern needs. customElements.define registers it, and the presenter (a plain object or module) is injected by the host page or by the element's owner, so the element stays reusable and free of application logic. Prefer this when screens are composed as elements across pages; the plain object view remains simpler for a single-page screen.
pitfalls: Constructors of custom elements must not inspect children or attributes; do wiring in connectedCallback, and expect it to run again after a move or re-insertion.
Event listeners added on the element itself survive re-rendering of its children; re-query child nodes inside the handlers instead of caching them in the constructor.
The element name must be globally unique and hyphenated; colliding definitions throw and leave the page with an unupgraded element.
